It's a real text re-read, not edited, which SDF's rule permits only as a character's claim, the way the final conversation treats the films. Don't build a plot step on a real document's "hidden" meaning.

35. Does anything here change the four mechanisms' standing in ADDENDUM 05? C moves from "does not work as a Part Two engine" to "works when James acts on a layer and pays, breaks on paper, and has a floor." A stays the gap (Illuminatus barely uses it). B is confirmed as something the organization runs on James (tailored versions, 02). D: nothing to build. Note the book's D inverted: Joe gets every key and declines (07), as James declines the lower door.

36. Any contradictions in the notes I should know about? Four. (1) "Never by deduction" (02, 07) against Joe's "I read all the clues" (07) and "the hero's doubt" as a break (03); see Q4. (2) 08 says the fifth Primus is "still unnamed" at the start of Trip 10, but in 07 Joe has already named Hagbard. Read it as Joe knowing and George not yet. (3) Cartwright appears on the Illuminati side in Trip 2 ("We let Celine's crowd take Dorn," 01) and as Hagbard's messenger in Trip 10 (08). That's deliberate in the book, but cite with care. (4) The diagnosis is called the organization's reply (02) though the doctor is Joe; see Q11.

reviews.file: 08 Research/Comps/STRUCTURE 01 — the mechanism and the chain.md
reviews.title: Structure 01 — the mechanism and the chain
reviews.intro:
15 Nov 2026. What this is built from: THE BOOK v8.2, the v8 brief, REVIEW 01 and 02, ADDENDUM 05, the thirteen engine maps, RESEARCH 01 and 02, the MindBook brief, The List, and the v6 to v8 drafts.

The mechanism is two copies. James's trade is to put two versions of one thing side by side and ask a dull question about the difference. The organization's whole method is to make sure there is only ever one copy of anything true: one printing, one account of a death, one helper who knows one task, one person who remembers something and has nobody to compare it with. It never blocks him. It agrees with him and then reissues the thing in a duller version. But a reissue is a second copy, and a second copy is the one thing James knows how to read. So every answer they give him is his next clue, and that is what forces each step.

What James does at every step is one of his work verbs, done to a person or a system: compare, capture, build a watcher, ask a dull question, sign, wait, tell. Each one leaves his name somewhere, because asking is what gets counted, and going quiet is counted as worse. He cannot stop without that being read. In the first half he checks things. From the pub on, he checks people.

The leak is your High Castle idea cut down to one kind: some people carry the last minutes of the life before this one, a place and a hand, and sometimes what the person holding the hand said. One person with that is a man who has not slept. Two people whose accounts match are evidence. The organization exists to stop the second copy turning up, on paper or in a person.

It stays funny because the method is office work on both sides: forms, tickets, a kennel booking, a flask. The plan's events, the win, Ana's pills and your four chapters stay. What changes is the middle of Part Two, the phone, the December appointment, and what the forty-one edits are for.

items.title: 1.1 The loop
items.html: Every step runs the same way. James holds two versions of one thing that should match and do not. He does one thing from his trade to check the difference. The check needs a person, who has a reason to help and a reason not to. The check is seen. The organization answers by agreeing and reissuing: a new owner for the job, a kind account of the death, a form that explains him. The reissue is a new second copy, so he has a new difference to check. You can test any chapter with it: what are the two copies, what does he do, who chooses, what do they reissue. The comparing comes from The Club Dumas ("El número Uno y el número Dos"), where a second copy opens doors that money does not. The reissue comes from Orwell (I.iv), where every edit is filed as a correction.

items.title: 1.2 What counts as a step
items.html: A step is James doing one verb to a person or a system and leaving with an object he did not have. The verbs are compare, capture, build, ask, test, sign, wait, tell, refuse. A chapter in which he only reads paper that someone handed him is not a step, and Part Two has eight of those. The fix in each is the same: he makes the comparison himself, or he asks for the thing by name. In Pattern Recognition every clue is an object a person hands over at a personal price (the napkin, ch. 17). Join each step to the next with "therefore" or "but". If only "and then" fits, the chapter is a delivery.

items.title: 1.3 What a step costs
items.html: Every check writes his name somewhere. That is already your machine: the payload counts people who ask. So the price list is concrete and rises: a row on the list, a form in his file, his initials on their annex, a post he must delete, a friend who has walked his garden, a dog. The second rule is King's (11/22/63, ch. 17 and 23): the bill lands on whoever opened the door, through a channel James opened himself. Noor pays for his visit. Buddy pays for the barbecue. The eighth address pays for his rule. James has to say so each time, in one sentence, or the reader thinks he has not noticed.

items.title: 1.4 Their answer is the next clue
items.html: The organization never refuses and never threatens. It does four things, in order, from your List: correct, ridicule, buy, vanish. Each of the first three produces paper. A correction is a second printing. A ridicule is his own post with bloodlines added. A purchase is a role already ticked, a seat, a friend. The Name of the Rose (Day 2, Terce) has the small version: the catalog lies about a book's status, never about its existence. So when James is stuck, the writer's question is what they just reissued and where the old version still sits. The old version is always somewhere, because your 1931 chapter says a clean plate is a confession.

items.title: 1.5 Five layers, each a true small conspiracy
items.html: A publisher's fraud (the edit). An employer watching staff (the count, told to helpers as "honeypot"). Executives buying a lifeboat (the seats, told as "disaster recovery"). Records and people moved (the schedule, told as "conservation" and "heritage"). And the floor: recall. Each is real, each is what one tier is told, and each covers the next. Illuminatus! (Trip 8) gives the condition: a layer drives the plot only when someone acts on it as if it were the bottom, and pays. So James signs the seat annex believing the seats are the point, and he builds the sheets on it. The seats break on a document in "What was on the phone", not on a speech.

items.title: 1.6 Two clocks
items.html: His is the second of December, an appointment he inherited from a dead man, and then the Monday. Theirs is the review date, and it moves only twice: in "A car park", because he signed a form and went quiet at work, and in "The leak". Quiet is the verb that moves it, which is why he cannot stop: in Lot 49 (ch. 5) the heroine tries to quit and quitting produces evidence. Write one calendar: reading room Monday 2 December, dinner Friday 6, sheets 7 to 19, leak Friday 20 (review brought from 31 December to Monday 23), envelopes Sunday 22. The other two date-moves in the plan go.

items.title: 1.7 The gate
items.html: In "Enjoy it while it lasts" James tries the winning move too early. He tells Saskia what the job does, guesses wrong about what she was told, and she hears a man who needs sleep. He writes one rule: I tell nobody until I know what they were told and can put their own paper in front of them. That is King's gate (ch. 3 and 7), set by the hero after a failure. It costs: three addresses resolve and a fourth is emptied while he keeps it. It opens only when a person gives him the list of what each helper was told. Libra sets its limit: a key gets a helper talking, it does not decide for them.

items.title: 1.8 The midpoint
items.html: "On land" is chapter 28 of 56 and your plan already puts the switch there: he invents a book. Before the pub he tests paper and systems. After it he tests people, and each James chapter opens on a test he set and its result: the control on Frank, the watcher, the kennel booked for the printed date, the slip on the old man's table, the half sentence posted to strangers. Eco's rule (Foucault's Pendulum, ch. 75 and 76) holds for all of them: one item, one hook, a readout through another person, and a price he cannot take back.

items.title: 2.1 Verdict: yes, one kind
items.html: What leaks is recall: the last minutes of the life before this one. Not other realities, not earlier societies, not objects. Your funeral chapter already has it (cold mud, a cracked hand), the floor night pays it, and the organization's own word for what it counts is "recall" (Utrecht, the job name, the invoice). The world before reaches the book only through people who carried it. That is who the givers were. Both maps say the idea works only if it stays this narrow, and I agree with them.

items.title: 2.2 What it contains, and the tell
items.html: A place, the weather, a hand, and sometimes what the owner of the hand said. Never history, never a prediction, never a fact about the organization. James gets a hand and no words, twice, and no third time, which keeps him from becoming a seer. The words reach him from other people. PLACEHOLDER, the tell: for a minute afterward one hand goes cold and the person tucks it under the other arm or sits on it. Small and a little ridiculous. It is why Kalder's note on James reads "Hands". Alternative: no bodily tell, and handlers judge by talk alone.

items.title: 2.3 Who has it, and the second witness
items.html: Anyone can, mostly near a death, which is why the count watches the bereaved and why his referral says "bereavement". Most people file it under no sleep. The second witnesses, in order: Noor (her hand, in "Leiden"), Marijke for Henk ("The other ten"), Els for her father, strangers on the forum ("The sheets"), Anneke at her door, and Ana in the Epilogue. Each tells him in their own words before he tells them his.

items.title: 2.4 What makes it checkable
items.html: Three checks, all in his trade. His watcher shows that forum posts which ask are left alone, while posts which describe a last minute are dressed up within days and their authors stop. Henk's words, written down in Marijke's kitchen, rhyme with Els's father's saying. And in "The sheets" he posts the first half of the sentence and strangers finish it, which is a challenge and a response. Then, at midnight, the paper copy matches. PLACEHOLDER, the sentence: "Don't be afraid. Hold on to whoever is holding your hand." Alternative: your own wording, same length, said by the living to the dying.

items.title: 2.5 How it makes the forty-one one edit, and gives the motive
items.html: Each edit removes, from a dull trustworthy book, a report that something was received or handed on: transmitted to arisen, shared to coincident, remembered to imagined. The exotic versions stay in every bookshop. What goes is the plain version a sensible person could check his own memory against. A recall is a copy and a sober page is the second copy. The motive follows. PLACEHOLDER: the people at the top remember on purpose and come back to their chair, and a world where ordinary people compare what they remember would not keep the chair for them. Some last minutes also have a polite man with a list in them.

items.title: 2.6 What the organization does about leaks
items.html: It counts people who say one aloud. It reclassifies them: grief, sleep, a counselor. Online it adds bloodlines. It buys the ones worth having, which is what the five seats are. It visits the rest, and the visit is meant to end in a sale, a move or silence. Killing is a handler's mistake. It also pays for the ceremonial and the ridiculous versions in years when too few people ask, which is your thermostat.

items.title: 2.7 What it must never become
items.html: No object leaks. No book changes by itself, or "Leiden, 1931" is unnecessary and the edit stops being evidence of an editor. No vision on demand: the floor works on the night he stops trying. No public event on a date. No machine and no physics behind it. A recall never appears on a sheet as a claim, because the sheets are paper. The reset stays offstage and in the past. The List needs entries 3, 7 and 17 rewritten as verbs of receiving, or "all forty-one are one edit" is false.

items.title: 3.1 Ana
items.html: She wants her grandmother to be okay and her husband to stop having one thing he tells her and one he does not. She holds the one skill he lacks: she reads people and upside-down paper faster than he reads systems, and in the Epilogue she holds the other half of the hand. She opens when he labels what he cannot prove, six times. It costs her a home, then a crime with her mother's pills. Role: the ally who is also his auditor. Scenes: "The math" (breakfast), "The schedule", "Twenty minutes", "The dinner", "The night before", Epilogue. She is well used. Give her one more job: in "Twenty minutes" she is the one who names his tell.

items.title: 3.2 Frank
items.html: He wants not to be a mug, and he wants the future to be good. He holds the two-column method and the 1953 text, and he was told "honeypot" with the rest of the team, which he repeats on the stairs. That makes him a helper by the smallest margin and earns him a sheet. He opens when he finds the cold years himself in accounts nobody handed James. It costs him his name beside James's on a ticket. Role: skeptic. Scenes: "Frank's kitchen", "The gorilla mask", "Frank, loose", "The sheets", "Leave it".

items.title: 3.3 Kalder, called Julian
items.html: He wants the seat, because when he crossed he found nobody holding his hand, and a chair is the only continuity on offer to him. He likes James. He holds the list of what every helper was told. He opens it once, awake, for himself: burned by a photograph, he gives James as long as his flask lasts, so that the organization is busy with James and slow with him. It costs James a gift from the man who poisoned his dog. Role: false ally. Scenes: "A round with a stranger", "The corporate day", "On land", "The gorilla mask", "The dinner", "A market, Sunday".

items.title: 3.4 Pieter
items.html: He wants a quiet team and safe children. He holds the right to rename a job, the word he was told, and the signature on James's access. He says "leave it" twice: at stand-up, and when James brings him the names with no HR record. He opens when he sees Lotte and Bas "per allocation" beside a desk sold four times. He then does one thing of his own: he hands his sheet to the man at his door. Role: gatekeeper. Scenes: "Leave it", "The week it vanished", "The money", "The corporate day", "The sheets", "The leak", "Leave it" (the last chapter).

items.title: 3.5 Saskia
items.html: Underused, so give her the failure. She wants clean access reviews and no blame. She holds the grant log and the ruleset tickets. In "The money" she tells him his role came through already ticked. In "Enjoy it while it lasts" he tells her what page 212 hides, guesses her reason wrong, and she logs it with a kind note about sleep. In "The sheets" she opens because he brings her the one line in her own log she did not write. She gives him the service account that ticked it. Role: the gatekeeper who files him as a crank first. Do not move her or punish her.

items.title: 3.6 Noor
items.html: She wants to stay alive, keep her mother's care-home place, and have Hendrik turn out right. She holds the 2009 photocopy, entry 26, the rule, Kalder's face and the shelfmark by heart. She has crossed. She breaks her rule to write to James for one reason: his public post will get him visited, and she wants it down. She opens when he deletes it first. Role: the ally who looks like an opponent, and his mirror, the Quiet. It costs her an afternoon with a clipboard. Scenes: "Leiden", "The vet", "Leiden, Friday", the repaired page in "Leave it".

items.title: 3.7 Els
items.html: She wants people to stop being polite about her father, and she wants him to have been sane. She holds the folder and what he used to say when they buried a dog. James arrives carrying the neighbor's kind version and loses her in a minute. She opens a week later because of the bucket line, which he took for Beard Man's nonsense and she knows as her father's. Role: gatekeeper turned witness. Scenes: "The math", "The sheets". She needs nothing more.

items.title: 3.8 Beard Man
items.html: He wants to be listened to and to do as little as possible. He holds two things he does not know he holds: the bucket theory is the professor's, improved, and he sells whole lots only because a polite man once asked him to telephone if anyone wanted a single title. Selling everything at once means he never has to ring. So the organization's one mistake is a lazy helper. Role: the clown who is right once, and the comic instrument Part Three lacks. Scenes: "Reading with a pen", "The week it vanished", a market beat in "The sheets", and his stall in "A market, Sunday".

items.title: 3.9 The Groningen dealer and the Deventer neighbor
items.html: Both were told "conservation" and both telephone. The dealer wants to be thought careful. He opens because James is plain about his reasons, and his silence afterward is what makes the organization tidy the job. The neighbor wants to have been a good neighbor. She holds the kind account of the professor's last months, believes it, and asks James whether Hendrik wrote to him too. She is a false ally who does not know it, and her call is how they learn he went to the daughter. Scenes: "Leave it" (the letter), "Groningen", "The math", a line each in "The sheets".

items.title: 3.10 Marijke, the widow in Zwolle
items.html: She wants one person to say Henk was not distracted. She holds the flask and Henk's exact words about his father and a bridge. She opens to a man with an old dog who says he is from nobody. James asks what Henk said, word for word, and writes it down. It costs her the question he cannot answer, whether Henk is somewhere. Role: the second witness, and the one source that did not reach him through the program. Scenes: "A pension visit, Zwolle" (offstage), "The other ten", "The sheets".

items.title: 3.11 Aylin
items.html: She wants the archive used properly and the cards to be true. She holds the visitor book and the catalog. For nine years, since the Leiden transfer brought her the collection, she has not asked what the last column means. Her own discovery is small: on the second of December she is made to write "in conservation" on James's slip for an item she knows is sound on its shelf. She opens at midnight by striking that status through. Role: gatekeeper. Scenes: the opening, "The drill" (through glass), "The reading room, continued", "The sheets", "The night before", "The final conversation". Fold the site manager into one line of hers.

items.title: 3.12 Anneke de Wit
items.html: She wants the bank to survive its own paperwork and not to be anyone's fool. She holds the signature on the invoice and the schedule, and the board. In December the old man brings her to watch a recruitment and reads James's referral aloud for her benefit, so she hears a bereaved man with a hobby. She opens to her own thirty signatures, outcomes he checked himself, and one row of the reason column that is hers. Role: the opponent who becomes the chair. Scenes: the opening, "The reading room, continued", "The sheets", "The night before", "Monday", "The final conversation".

items.title: 3.13 The old man
items.html: He wants to come back to the same chair, and he likes an audience. He holds the reason and the paper copy of the sentence. He opens only when it no longer matters. He opposes by kindness: thanks, an offer, a status on a card. Make him the head of one region who is addressed as the head. Anneke says it in "Monday": they are all called that. This is the MindBook's best unused find and it settles the scale problem. Scenes: the opening, "The reading room, continued", "The final conversation".

items.title: 3.14 Bram
items.html: He wants the count to be accurate and the work to be decent, and he has never had what he counts. The plan says he "will go himself" and then gives him nowhere to go. Send him to Pieter's door in "The leak". He likes lists, he drinks the tea, and he reads Pieter's sheet at Pieter's table, where he learns from a helper that the desks are sold four times. He folds it into his folder and carries on. Role: the mirror at the professional level. Scenes: "A room with a long table", "The long table, again", "The leak".

items.title: 3.15 The brewery man
items.html: He wants to be in. He holds five seats, a desk with his name at the drill, and no HR record, which makes him the result of James's reconciliation. Shown that his desk is on three other lists, he says "You don't get it. I'm in," because each of the four believes he is the real one. He reports. Role: the opponent by money, and the cause of the leak. Scenes: "The drill" (a name on a desk), "The money", "The sheets", "The leak". Keep him on the list.

items.title: 3.16 The forum and the quiet ones
items.html: The forum wants company and to be believed. It holds the second copies: strangers with a last minute of their own. It is also farmed, and James proves that with his watcher. He uses it four times, each as a test: the deleted question posted in "The payload", the page-118 query in "The math", the correction at the barbecue, and the half sentence in "The sheets". The quiet ones open to that half sentence and to nothing else. Role: chorus and second witness. Cut Verhoef's grandson and the archivist's daughter as named people; let them be two of the replies.

items.title: 3.17 The dogs
items.html: Buddy wants the kitchen floor and James. He is the detector James trusts and cannot cite: four hours away from Julian, the growl at the dinner. He is the reason for the no (five seats, no dogs), the bill for the barbecue, and the person the sentence is finally said to. Mora goes where Ana goes and rides in the back on the night before. Write the rule the way the v8 draft found it: every table James sits at has a dog under it, and the organization's tables never do. Mora is under Frank's table, since Buddy cannot do Frank's stairs.

items.title: 4.1 The reading room
items.html: Sharpen. James wants to keep a dead man's appointment. He drives there alone and is told he was expected. On the tray is the printer's 1931 ledger, open at the order for page 118: one line struck, one written beside it. The old man mentions the seats, left findable. PLACEHOLDER: cut "you were counted the night you asked" here, because it spends "The payload". Alternative: keep it and accept that. What the reader gets is a place, a date, a silent woman and a generator. Therefore everything after is how he came to be at that table, and what he asks for when the scene resumes.

items.title: 4.2 The funeral
items.html: Keep. Yours. He wants to get Ana through the day. He says yes at the grave without having checked, and he gets the flash: mud and a cracked hand, filed under no sleep. This is the first copy of the leak, held by a man with nothing to compare it to. It costs him the feeling of being a fraud in the one area where he never is one. Therefore he has to check the sentence he confirmed.

items.title: 4.3 The good life
items.html: Keep. Yours. He wants ordinary life back. He describes his trade, which is the method of the whole book: watch a system, compare what it says with what it does, ask the dull question. The bank line goes in here. He finds fourteen tabs about dying. Therefore the search has started without him deciding to start it.

items.title: 4.4 Reading with a pen
items.html: Keep. Yours. He wants the question answered by reading. He types a question on the forum and deletes it, which is the ask he cannot yet make. Beard Man will sell only the whole lot, so he takes forty-odd books home, the thin one among them, and hears the bucket theory. It costs him two bags and Ana's wrong idea of what the notebook is about. Therefore the lot is in his kitchen and he goes through it spine by spine.

items.title: 4.5 The sentence
items.html: Keep. Yours. He wants to see what the professor scribbled on. He compares his copy with the first impression, line by line, and finds three edits of one kind with the typos left in. He asks "where else?" It costs him a night. Therefore he needs a control, another copy of the 1931 printing, and the only way to get one is to write to dealers.

items.title: 4.6 Down House, 1860
items.html: Keep. A real book changed between printings by its own author. Fix the dates per REVIEW 01, and let the chapter say that Darwin added a hand where James's printer removed one.

items.title: 4.7 A round with a stranger
items.html: Sharpen. He wants his Wednesday. Open on one line: on Monday he wrote to three dealers for a 1931 copy. He is paired with Julian, who asks about Buddy first and says he is in continuity: if your building burns down, who does your payroll on Monday. James tells him the dog's name and that he reads old books. That is the cost, and he does not know it. The reader learns later that the letter is why the man is on that tee. Therefore, on Thursday, James being James, he checks what would in fact run on Monday.

items.title: 4.8 Utrecht, 1993
items.html: Keep. It gives the reader the word "recall", the two lunches and the seats without the mother, thirty years before James meets any of them. The reader is one step ahead from here on, which is where the dread and the jokes come from.

items.title: 4.9 Leave it
items.html: Sharpen. He wants the answer to Julian's question, so he reads the full job list and finds one with no owner at 02:14. He raises it at stand-up, in front of nine people, and reads Pieter's pause. He opens a ticket. The dealer's reply arrives with the postscript about being plain. Three weeks later continuity wants "the person who reads things", which is the organization buying before it does anything else. It costs him eleven words said aloud. Therefore, since Pieter's sentence about the migration is false, he captures what the job sends.

items.title: 4.10 The payload
items.html: Change. He wants to know what forty kilobytes are. He captures them: employee numbers and two-word reasons. One verb he cannot place, "recalled", and he takes it for a product term. At the bottom is his own number, "asked (job)". Then he searches and finds an older row, "wrote (dealer)", eleven days before stand-up. So he sends a test input, as he would at work: he posts the question he deleted in the spring. The next night there is a third row, "posted (forum)". It costs him the shame he avoided, and now the bank knows his handle. Therefore two questions: who told them about a letter, and is the edit a one-off.

items.title: 4.11 The control case
items.html: Keep. He wants to kill his finding. The 1931 copy arrives from Groningen, expensive, and he lies to Ana about the price. Same three edits, so it is the whole run. Nine other books show nothing. Then the thin book: two hands, forty-one edits, his sentence at eleven, and on the last page a reference, the second of December and "Ask". It costs him money and a small lie. Therefore he has a date, and one living person connected to both the book and his row: the dealer.

items.title: 4.12 The week it vanished
items.html: Change. Move it to the end of Part One, after "Groningen", and make the plate dirty. He wants to see the job again. It has been renamed, given an owner and a boring ticket, and his ticket is closed against one that now exists, backdated. Only his screenshot shows the old name. Beard Man tells him how the professor died. James asks Pieter one dull question: who owns it now? "Continuity. Which is you, as of the first." It costs him the hope that this is an error. Therefore he walks into Part Two holding a thin book, a date, and a job on their program.

items.title: 4.13 A pension visit, Zwolle
items.html: Keep. The villain alone: a kind afternoon, a borrowed car, a canal. Add two things the chain needs: the visitor pours his own coffee from a flask, and he asks Henk, lightly, whether he recalls anything else. Inside the organization this death is the exception people are uneasy about.

items.title: 4.14 Groningen
items.html: Sharpen. Move it before "The week it vanished". He wants to know who reported a letter. He drives there and is plain about his reasons. The dealer asks who sent him, then explains: polite people in 2011, a telephone number, a kindness to old books. James tells him what the call does. The dealer says he will not make another. James gets the first word a helper was told, "conservation", and the first proof that telling works. It costs the dealer: he is now seen not telephoning. Therefore the organization tidies the job, and James learns that his telling caused it.

items.title: 5.1 Deventer, March
items.html: Keep. The professor broke his own rule and wrote to them. Add that his letter named the shelfmark and asked to consult it, and was given the December sitting. Then Noor's "nobody has ever simply asked" stays true: he argued, in writing. The visitor photographs the notebook, so later only the original is worth taking.

items.title: 5.2 Croton, 530 BC
items.html: Keep. Tell it as what it is, a rival's verse mocking Pythagoras: the oldest surviving mention of the idea, already with a mask on.

items.title: 5.3 Frank's kitchen
items.html: Sharpen. He wants someone who will try to kill what he has, because at work only a screenshot stands. He debunks Frank's three theories, asks why a dead theory gets a documentary, and gets Frank's two columns and the 1953 text. He copies the method: one column for what he could show a stranger, one for what only he has seen. On the stairs Frank says the job is a honeypot; Pieter told the team. Mora is under the table. Therefore: a security trap would not read book dealers, so Pieter was told something false, and the thin book is in the wrong column until a second person vouches for it. The daughter.

items.title: 5.4 The math
items.html: Change. He wants a witness to the professor. He goes to Deventer first, and the neighbor gives him the kind version: unwell, not sleeping. He carries it to the shop, says he is sorry about the illness, and Els shows him out. Buddy will not get up, and James tells him the bucket line. A week later she rings: her father said that. She gives him the folder. He does the arithmetic. PLACEHOLDER: "a better place" is on the preferred side. Then, in place of withdrawing, he tests the template: he posts the page-118 difference as a plain query. Breakfast with Ana stays. Therefore an answer is coming, and he knows what it should say.

items.title: 5.5 The corporate day
items.html: Sharpen. He wants one day off. In the car park Pieter kindly hands him a wellbeing referral with the reason already filled in: bereavement, sleep, preoccupation with historical documents. So the bank knows about his books. He has just read "agreed with and then reclassified", and he signs it on the hood of the car. Julian sees. On the course he asks one dull question, who decides who gets a seat, and gets "the client; we count chairs." Fix "from the spring" to June. It costs him a form in his file. Therefore he stops raising things at work, and that evening the polite correction arrives, paragraph for paragraph.

items.title: 5.6 A car park
items.html: Keep. The handler reports that the subject signed and has stopped asking. The voice corrects him: stopped out loud, which is worse. This is the first of the two date moves, and it comes from a form James chose to sign. Stay anonymous; the reader is told who it is two chapters later.

items.title: 5.7 Leiden
items.html: Sharpen. He wants to know who else has seen the template. He has posted the reply beside the folder's wording, and Noor writes to tell him to take it down before it gets him visited. He deletes his own evidence, and then she gives him an address. In her kitchen she confirms the template, entry 26 and the rule. She says the thing REVIEW 01 needs: it is in every bookshop; they remove the plain version you would believe. He notices her hand under her arm and asks why. "Hendrik asked me that." Wrong column; find the money; the reference is the depot's format. Therefore the building his program drills in holds the appointment.

items.title: 5.8 Mexico City, 1994
items.html: Keep. Facts only, plus one sentence in which the narrator declines to connect a real man's disappearance to anything in this book.

items.title: 5.9 The drill
items.html: Sharpen. He wants to see the building. At desk forty he does what he does at any recovery test: he counts. Forty staff came on the bus, and there are more named desks than lanyards. He writes down the names with no person. Through the shut glass door he matches the format on a spine to the thin book's last page. He asks the site manager who is upstairs: "Heritage. Different tenant, same generator." Julian waves from the car park, having watched him look at the glass. Therefore: who are the desks for, and who pays for a generator two tenants share.

items.title: 5.10 The money
items.html: Change. He wants the owners of the empty desks. His first program task is to reconcile Annex C against HR and sign it off. Saskia says his role came through already ticked, dated the week of his ticket. He finds names with no HR record, the brewery man among them, and takes them to Pieter: vendor allocations, sign. He reads "companion animals are not accommodated", thinks of Buddy in the car, and signs. That evening he pulls thirty-one years of invoices himself and finds the foundation's line: recall index, per flagged person. He learns what he initialed one evening late. Therefore: if people are billed for, the renamed job still runs, and he goes to look.

items.title: 5.11 Enjoy it while it lasts
items.html: Change. He wants to see the job. The new tools have a rule on page 212 that hides exactly that shape, and his access is narrowed by it. He tells Saskia what the rule hides and guesses her reason wrong; she hears a man with a referral and logs it. He writes his rule. Days later, still narrowed, he takes Julian's tip to ask the name on the invoice. Julian K. fixes it in eleven minutes, and James notes that the narrowing and the fix bill from one address. Therefore: Julian can see his access, so what else can he see? James decides to find out.

items.title: 5.12 A room with a long table
items.html: Keep. Bram explains the two columns. Add two things: this is one region, with one handler to a bank, and the plan for James is to buy him. The schedule will reach him through the annex he signed. What he does with it is the test.

items.title: 5.13 Leiden, nine years ago
items.html: Keep. Kalder's crossing in Noor's kitchen. Add his line: when it went through him there was nobody there, so he asked for the seat. The date does not move in this chapter.

items.title: 5.14 On land
items.html: Keep. The midpoint. He wants to know whether Julian reads what he reads, because Julian has used a word from the professor's margin. He sets a trap as he would at work: he names a book that does not exist, and Julian knows it. The hearings are on the bar television, each admission paired with a finding of nothing. Ana tells the toaster story. It costs him a lie to a friend and a title he cannot take back. Therefore he needs Julian among other people, with a control, so when Ana asks for a barbecue he says yes and does not tell her why.

items.title: 5.15 The gorilla mask
items.html: Sharpen. He wants to watch Julian with witnesses. He drops the invented title on Frank in Julian's hearing: "sounds made up." Then he finds that the post he deleted for Noor is back under his name with bloodlines added. His correction reaches eleven people. Julian says "Deventer." Buddy keeps away four hours. Ana says keep him. That night James builds what he builds at work: a watcher that copies his threads and the forum's public pages at 02:14 and shows what changed. The cost is said in one sentence: Julian has now walked the back lane, the fourth gate and the bowl.

items.title: 5.16 The promise
items.html: Keep. PLACEHOLDER: same night, Ana coming downstairs at four. Alternative: by phone, later. He is frightened for a specific reason: they can write as him, so anything can be put in his name. He asks her to believe him on the day he says so, and to run. "Run where? I've got a Doberman." Then okay. Therefore she will know the sentence when she hears it.

items.title: 5.17 The schedule
items.html: Sharpen. The quarter's conservation transfers route to him because he signed the annex. He sees their address, a date eleven days off, and "companion". He asks Ana to go; she refuses; she reads it upside down; he tells her. She leaves the address, with Mora. Buddy cannot go: her mother's flat is up two flights. So James takes precautions. He adds the eleven addresses to the watcher from public notices, books Buddy into the vet's kennel for the week of the date, works from home, and puts a camera on the front door. Therefore the house is never empty by day, and he is guarding a date.

items.title: 5.18 Washington, 1953
items.html: Keep. Four days in January, not a weekend. Give the room here and leave the quoted sentence with Frank.

items.title: 5.19 A street, night
items.html: Keep. Kalder is to recover the original notebook. The car is in the drive on a weekday, so he cannot go in by day. Four days before the printed date he uses the back lane and the bowl. This is his own choice against the method, and it follows from James staying home.

items.title: 5.20 The vet
items.html: Sharpen. Two in the morning; the vet says they had him booked for Thursday. Home at six, the camera shows a quiet front door and the thin book is gone. James says it plainly: I watched the date and the door. He sends Noor the barbecue photo and she rings: Kalder, the library transfer, his own flask. In Leiden she says his post is back up. He shows her the watcher's record that he deleted it and they restored it. She still refuses to be a witness, writes the shelfmark from memory, and says ask in person, do not argue. Then a van on her street.

items.title: 5.21 Leiden, Friday
items.html: Keep. A clipboard and an afternoon. The reader sees the bill for James's visit before he hears of it.

items.title: 5.22 A corridor, sixteen
items.html: Keep. The motive: eleven questions not asked and a hand taken too late. Place it after "The other ten", directly before the floor.

items.title: 5.23 The night he stops being afraid
items.html: Sharpen. It now has a cause. He sits down because Henk's last minute, in Marijke's words, has the same shape as the thing he filed at the funeral, and a second copy is something he cannot file. Four nights. On the fourth he stops trying. He gets the hand, known all his life, and no words. He checks the kitchen like a system. He sees that the forty-one are one edit: each removes a report of something received. He rings Ana. Therefore he will tell her all of it once.

items.title: 5.24 Urfa, 1994
items.html: Keep. Say what moved: monumental building before farming. The book never says Tresidder found it.

items.title: 5.25 The long table, again
items.html: Keep. Kalder reports the crossing. He saw it on the Wednesday round, from the terrace: James alone, the old dog in the cart, looking at his own hands. "James has hands." No date moves. Bram authorizes the offer and says he will go himself when the time comes. The dog: yes, it was efficient, and the room does not like the answer.

items.title: 5.26 Twenty minutes
items.html: Keep. Exactly as planned: the tablecloth, every object, labels on what he cannot prove. The objects are now ones he made or signed: the captures with his three rows, the referral, the annex with his initials, the watcher's printouts, Henk's words, the flask, photographs where the thin book was. One addition: Ana tells him he sits on his hand, and learns where he was at her grandmother's grave. She asks about the next address, nine days off. He says his rule. "You made that up." "Yes." Six times "I don't know." She is coming home.

items.title: 5.27 The other ten
items.html: Change. Move it up, between "Leiden, Friday" and "A corridor, sixteen". His own alert goes off: a death notice at a listed address. He checks all ten against public records, which is the one thing nobody handed him: three resolved (a care home, a sale, Henk), four quiet. He rings Noor's workshop and a colleague says she has stopped taking private work. He drives to Zwolle with Buddy, asks Marijke what Henk said, word for word, and writes it down. She gives him the flask. He tells her nothing yet, and now he has a reason: the rule. Therefore the floor.

items.title: 5.28 The band
items.html: Merge. Fold it into "Frank, loose". The accounts against the years is the right finding, and it should be Frank who makes it. As a separate chapter it is James alone, reading, and right again.

items.title: 5.29 Frank, loose
items.html: Sharpen. He wants to know whether paper nobody handed him can move a skeptic, which is a dry run for the sheets. He brings the foundation's published accounts and lets Frank work. Frank finds the grants in the cold years himself, and one cold year with no grant, which neither can explain. The accounts show the same steps as the invoice. "I believe the invoice." During the evening the watcher reports the eighth address: house listed, owner moved to care. That is the price of the rule, and James says so. Cut the simulation talk. Therefore he goes to December with pulled paper only.

items.title: 5.30 Leiden, 1931
items.html: Keep. The visitor, the three lines, the misprints left in, two sons. It sits directly before the ledger is read, so the reader knows what the struck line is when James does not.

items.title: 5.31 The reading room, continued
items.html: Change. He asks first. He writes the reference on a slip and puts it on the table. The old man reads it: "He asked too." Aylin is told to mark it "in conservation." Then James takes both impressions from his bag, opens them at 118 on either side of the ledger, and collates the three in pencil. He lays down his findings. The old man thanks him for the cleanest annex in years and reads the referral aloud, for Anneke. Five seats, no dogs. No. He leaves the lower door shut. Therefore they send the friend.

items.title: 6.1 The dinner
items.html: Change. One beat changes. Ana is home and he wants an ordinary Friday. Kalder arrives uninvited, the organization's answer to no. Code, Buddy growling, "is Buddy okay now", the book you said you'd read, Burn Notice, the sentence he promised. Ana's pills, her idea. Kalder sleeps. James photographs him and the bag by the door. Nobody touches the phone. Kalder wakes and does the sum aloud: for that photograph he is retired. He unlocks the phone himself and pours coffee from his own flask. James has as long as the flask lasts. It is no favor: if they are busy with James they are slow with him.

items.title: 6.2 What was on the phone
items.html: Change. Kalder sits across the table while James reads: handlers by code, next quarter's schedule, the seats for four companies, and what each helper was told. James checks the gift against what he made himself. Three reasons match what Frank, the dealer and the site manager told him. And the desk numbers match the annex he reconciled: desk twelve is Pieter's and also three strangers'. The seats are sold four times. That is the lifeboat layer breaking on a document. Kalder takes the phone. "Too bad. I liked you." It costs James a gift from that man. Therefore the gate is open.

items.title: 6.3 Compartments
items.html: Merge. One paragraph at the end of "What was on the phone". The arithmetic was done in "The math" and the list is on the table. A chapter of understanding with no scene repeats both.

items.title: 6.4 The sheets
items.html: Sharpen. One page each: what you were told, what your own paper did, and your desk on three other lists. Pieter. Saskia, who gives him the service account. Anneke: thirty signatures, outcomes from his watcher, and a week of the reason column with numbers removed. Aylin: statuses in her own hand; she shows the visitor book. Marijke: the photograph of the man asleep, the flask on the table. Els. Frank. Beard Man at his stall, who was told to telephone and has a theory about that. The brewery man, who refuses. Himself, since he initialed the annex. And the forum: he posts half the sentence and eleven strangers finish it. Each person he tells is now counted, and he says so.

items.title: 6.5 The leak
items.html: Sharpen. The brewery man's report brings the review from the thirty-first to Monday, the second and last move. Three addresses get a visitor. Pieter rings from his car. Let him in, make tea, say nothing. The man is Bram, who likes lists, and Pieter, on his own, hands him the sheet. Bram learns from a helper that the desks are oversold. Anneke is due to sign the quarter's schedule on Monday and the board has seen nothing. Therefore twelve envelopes in two days.

items.title: 6.6 The night before
items.html: Sharpen. Ana drives, Mora in the back, twelve doors. PLACEHOLDER: cut the handler's house by mistake. At midnight Aylin lets him in to copy the visitor book, strikes "in conservation" from his slip, and brings the item: an invented letter from Tresidder, Urfa, 1929, giving the sentence as it was said to him. It matches Henk's and the eleven. He copies it by hand and leaves it there. At six Anneke opens before he knocks, hand under her arm. One row was hers. She asks if it is true. "A hand, twice. I don't know." "Go home."

items.title: 6.7 Monday
items.html: Keep. The sixth green, the old dog, the phone face down. The vote is imagined, and that is in character now that the last thing he did was answer her question. Anneke's call adds two lines. The old man ran this region; they are all called the head. And the reason he lives, corrected: they have killed, rarely, and each time it was somebody's mistake; now two hundred people hold their own names. He agrees and asks one last thing.

items.title: 6.8 The final conversation
items.html: Change. There is an object on the table: the letter he asked for, brought by Aylin because the request stands, and the thin book, returned. The old man talks around it. Lead with the only news: they do it on purpose, to come back. He reads James's pencil copy and changes one word. The films are short boasts, and James laughs. On the seats James gets there first: desk twelve. Then his callback: it was for leaving, not staying. Anneke's reason, the deal, his doubt about a story this neat. No dog under this table.

items.title: 6.9 A market, Sunday
items.html: Sharpen. Set it at Beard Man's market. Kalder is found by his bag: James told them what he carries and the three places that fit it. PLACEHOLDER: closing in means the seat he asked for, a desk and a bed on the lower floor, no course and no dogs. Alternative: leave it unsaid. James rings. You shouldn't have touched my dog. Kalder half smiles. Count the clubs to fourteen.

items.title: 6.10 Leave it
items.html: Keep. The date passes. The invoice steps down. He and Frank file one dull ticket against page 212. Pieter asks whether he is still on the list, and James tells him nobody is kept, the ones on it included. The repaired page comes from Leiden. He switches the watcher off. The book he may publish claims nothing; give it a last page of real, checkable things with their sources.

items.title: 6.11 Epilogue
items.html: Sharpen. Four years on, a quarter past two, the blankets. He holds Buddy's paw and says the sentence, which is the instruction used once, on the page. The garden by the gate. "He's in a better place. I'll see him soon." That week Ana, half asleep, says his hands were cracked at the knuckles and she knew them. He writes it in the thin book as a forty-second entry with no before and no after, and tells nobody. Page 212 is gone. Ida sits at the stairs, and he cannot check that one.

sections.title: 7. What the organization does, step by step

items.title: 7.1 Before the book
items.html: In March a visitor photographs the professor's notebook and decides to wait. The furniture is to be bought later. The dealers who knew him are asked to telephone about single titles. Beard Man, to save himself the trouble, sells everything as one lot before the van comes. That is the one mistake, and it is why the original notebook is in James's kitchen.

items.title: 7.2 The letter
items.html: James writes to three dealers for the 1931 printing. Groningen telephones. The name is matched to an employer that pays for the count, and the nightly job writes "wrote (dealer)". A handler is told to get near. The method is the vacuum cleaner from your MindBook brief: ten minutes, no notes, ask about the dog. Kalder's one careless line about payroll sends James to the job list.

items.title: 7.3 Stand-up
items.html: "Asked (job)" is a category of one. The invoice steps the following Monday. The first answer is the gentlest on the list: Pieter's sentence, then the program. They ask for the person who reads things, because a reader inside the program is easier to watch and can be offered something.

items.title: 7.4 Groningen goes quiet
items.html: A helper who stops telephoning has been told something. They conclude James knows what the calls are for. So the job is renamed, given an owner and a ticket, and James's own ticket is closed against it. His program role is ticked the same week by a service account. From here on, what he finds at work was placed where a new joiner would see it.

items.title: 7.5 The daughter and the post
items.html: The neighbor reports the Deventer visit. The page-118 query gets paragraph one of the template. At work he is reclassified with a referral. When he signs and goes quiet, the handler reports "stopped asking", and the review comes forward to the end of the year. Kalder is told to learn what he loves.

items.title: 7.6 Recruitment
items.html: He is given the annex to reconcile and signs it. The tools narrow his access by one shape. Kalder offers the fix and delivers it in eleven minutes, the problem and the rescue from one address. Bram says to let the schedule reach him. What he does with it will show whether he can be bought.

items.title: 7.7 The pub and the garden
items.html: Kalder nods at a book that does not exist, and knows by the barbecue that he was tested, so he tests back. The deleted post is restored and dressed, which is paragraph four of the template. At the barbecue he learns the lane, the gate and the bowl. He likes the evening.

items.title: 7.8 The house
items.html: The order is to recover the original notebook. James is home every day, so Kalder poisons the bowl four days early to get him out at night. Nobody above him asked for that. Noor has been seen with James twice, and she is made quiet in an afternoon. The visit to their address is struck from the next schedule, because the dog lived and the book is back.

items.title: 7.9 The crossing and the offer
items.html: Kalder sees it on a Wednesday and files it. The offer is authorized: five seats. On the second of December the old man brings the bank's head of risk to watch, reads the referral aloud so that she hears a bereaved man, and has the slip marked "in conservation". James says no. The friend is sent to close.

items.title: 7.10 The end
items.html: A handler photographed asleep at a subject's table is finished, and Kalder knows it before they do. The brewery man reports the sheets. The review is pulled to Monday, visitors go to three doors, a van follows a car and gives up. The bank's board removes the trustees. The head of the region is retired. Kalder is found by his clubs and given his seat.

sections.title: 8. What to cut, and what not to touch

items.title: 8.1 Cut the thumb
items.html: The largest document in the book cannot be taken from a drugged man. Ana's pills stay, because they are hers. The photographs are what the sleep is for. The phone is opened by its owner, awake, for his own reasons.

items.title: 8.2 Cut the erased backups
items.html: A job wiped from every backup is the cleanest plate in the book and contradicts "Leiden, 1931". Rename it. Then the last chapter's "the job is gone in a month" and page 212 both make sense, because the job has been running all along.

items.title: 8.3 Cut "Compartments" and "The band" as chapters
items.html: The first is an understanding with no scene. The second is James alone being right. Their content survives inside "What was on the phone" and "Frank, loose". Part Two drops to thirty chapters and loses one of its reading chapters.

items.title: 8.4 Cut two date moves and four tells
items.html: The date moves in "A car park" and "The leak" only. Kalder's tells are three: the word, the nod, "Deventer". The consultancy on the seat contract is unnamed. Julian K. is played as a favor James can see through, not a clue he files. The four key-holders become one question to Pieter.

items.title: 8.5 Cut the second and third cosmologies
items.html: Keep the pool and the bucket. Cut the warden who calls himself God and the simulation that renders what is observed. "Within" against "through us" is a translation dispute Noor points at, never an edit. "Every book" is the old man's boast; the narration asserts forty-one.

items.title: 8.6 Cut what the reviews already dropped
items.html: No counselor, no appointment card, no hair on the thin book, no errand upstairs at the drill, no shelfmark said in a pub, no wrong film in the accounts, no Buddy at Frank's flat, no watch from a car at the eighth address, no catalog feed for the watcher. One build, two feeds: the forum and the addresses.

items.title: 8.7 Do not touch your four chapters or "Twenty minutes"
items.html: The method of the whole book is in "The good life" and "The sentence". "Twenty minutes" is the scene where his rule about labeling what he cannot prove earns a person. It gains three objects and loses nothing.

items.title: 8.8 Do not touch the win
items.html: Compartments attacked with each person's own paper, people who simply stop, some who do not, and a body that would confirm every envelope. The sheets gain one line, the desk sold four times, which lets them say what Part 0 promised.

items.title: 8.9 Do not touch the small objects or the order of what the reader knows
items.html: The flask, the bag by the door, the invented book and the promise to run are each planted once and paid once. The flask now pays three times. The reader learns who Kalder is before the pub. Keep that; the dread depends on it.

items.title: 8.10 Do not touch the floor night, the lower door, or the no
items.html: He does nothing for four nights, he never opens the door his badge opens, and he refuses five seats because of a dog. These are the three places where not acting is the act, and they work because everything around them is now something he did.

items.title: 9.1 The sentence
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. The choice: the words James reads at midnight and says to Buddy. I recommend an instruction from the living to the dying, under twelve words: "Don't be afraid. Hold on to whoever is holding your hand." Downstream: Marijke's version, Els's father's bucket saying, the eleven replies, the old man's one-word change and the Epilogue all quote or bend it. Nothing in either reading-room chapter or the Epilogue can be drafted until it exists.

items.title: 9.2 The tell
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. The choice: whether recall has a bodily sign. I recommend the cold hand tucked under an arm. Downstream: Noor in "Leiden", Marijke on Henk, Ana naming it in "Twenty minutes", Kalder's "Hands", Anneke at her door. Without it, handlers judge by talk, and those five beats need another way to let James recognize it in someone else.

items.title: 9.3 The line to Els
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. The choice: your decision 5. I recommend the bucket line, said to Buddy on the way out. Downstream: it makes Beard Man's one right theory the professor's, gives Beard Man a job in Part Three, and keeps James from having a third leak. Alternative: a sentence he has always said and never read, which is stronger and makes him a seer.

items.title: 9.4 The order of Part One's last three chapters
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend "Groningen", then "A pension visit, Zwolle", then "The week it vanished". Downstream: the dealer's silence causes the tidying, and the part ends on "Continuity. Which is you." Alternative: your order, in which the job vanishes for no reason James supplied and the part ends on a quiet talk.

items.title: 9.5 The count line in the opening
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend cutting it from page three and not moving it, since by December James has known for six months. Downstream: "The payload" keeps its turn. Alternative: keep it and let the payload be a confirmation.

items.title: 9.6 Who opens the phone
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend Kalder, awake, for the length of his flask. Downstream: "What was on the phone" becomes a two-hander, and everything on it must be checked against James's own annex. Alternative: the photographs are the whole prize and he learns each helper's reason by asking, which costs Part Three about three chapters.

items.title: 9.7 The thin book
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend stolen in "The vet", on the table in "The final conversation", returned. Downstream: one sentence changes in the brief, the photographs are on the tablecloth, and the Epilogue has a book to write in. Alternative: never taken, and the poisoning is only a message.

items.title: 9.8 What they want, and how big they are
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend: they come back, and they need the chair still there; and the old man heads one region. Downstream: REVIEW 01's motive and scale findings close, "buys the world time" becomes "a generation, in this part of the world", and Part 0's idea paragraph is rewritten to match the ending you wrote.

items.title: 9.9 Who gave
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend people: the ones who remembered, said so plainly, and taught the sentence. The book says no more than that. Downstream: nothing non-human anywhere, and Tresidder's letter records a custom, not a revelation. Alternative: leave it open on purpose, and say so in Part 0 so no draft answers it by accident.

items.title: 9.10 What James hopes for at the end
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend the meeting: he will know the hand. Ana's half-asleep line is the only matched pair in the book and he keeps it to himself. Ida at the stairs stays unchecked. Alternative: return, which makes Ida the answer and the pool a wheel.

items.title: 9.11 "A better place" on the style guide
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend putting the phrase on the preferred side of Els's folder, with the deprecated side showing only a shelfmark. Downstream: the lie at the grave becomes the machine's own wording, and the Epilogue needs him to say the sentence first and the phrase second. Alternative: leave the folder to books only.

items.title: 9.12 The eighth address
items.html: PLACEHOLDER. I recommend "moved to care, house listed", reported by his own watcher during "Frank, loose". Downstream: his rule has a price a reader can forgive. Alternative: dead, which he then carries to the last page, and "kills rarely" stops being true.

reviews.file: 08 Research/Comps/REVIEW 01 — the story, the concepts and the theories.md
reviews.title: Review 01 — the story, the concepts and the theories
reviews.intro:
15 Nov 2026. What was read: THE BOOK v8.2 (every line), the v8 brief, The List, the MindBook brief, and drafts v8/51–56, v7/45, v7/49, v8/52–53 to check claims.

The story makes sense as a chain of events. A man finds an edited sentence, finds a job that counts people who ask, is walked into the machine's own paperwork, loses his fear on a kitchen floor, and wins by handing ordinary people their own documents. That spine holds and nobody else has it. What does not yet hold is the thing the spine is about. The plan gives three different answers to "what did the edits take out," never says what the organisation gains by hiding it, and leaves the one deleted sentence as a placeholder, so the ending currently pays off a feeling and not a fact.

The three things that most need fixing. First, the central truth and the motive for hiding it (1.1, 1.2, 1.3). Second, Anneke: she sits in the opening hearing everything, then is turned weeks later by a sheet that tells her less than she heard (2.1). Third, the two biggest reveals of Part Three break your own rules: the phone is opened by drugging a man, and the truth arrives as a nine-item speech with nothing on the table (5.1, 5.2).

The three strongest. The win itself: compartments attacked with each helper's own paper, and "a body would confirm every envelope" (1.10). Ana ending the game herself with the pills after the promise to run. And the flask, the bag by the door and the invented book: small objects planted early that pay off cleanly (3.6).

items.title: 1.1 The forty-one edits mean three different things
items.html: In "The sentence" the edits turn given into arose: a claim about history, that someone handed knowledge to people. In Part 0 the deleted sentences "aren't history. They're instructions" for dying without fear. In "The night he stops being afraid" all forty-one "take out the thing that passes between people." The draft of "The final conversation" tries to join them ("We took the passing"), but Tresidder's page 118 is still a sentence about early peoples, not an instruction. Pick one meaning and make the other two follow from it. The cheapest join: the people who gave the knowledge were the ones who remember across lives, and what they gave was the method. Then history, instruction and "passing" are one thing, and it must be said once, plainly, before Part Three. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 1.2 The hidden thing is on sale in every bookshop
items.html: The plan's own research quotes the Tibetan and Egyptian books of the dead: published instructions for dying without fear and keeping yourself across the gap. So the organisation has not hidden what happens when we die. The plan has the answer but uses it only once, for the Dalai Lama search: "the ceremony that makes the real thing unthinkable." That is the real concept, and it is better than deletion: they do not remove the instruction, they make it exotic, ceremonial or funny. Say so early, through Noor, or the reader who owns a paperback Thödol stops believing on the spot. It also changes what the forty-one edits are for: they remove the ordinary versions, the ones in dry books a sensible person would trust. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 1.3 The motive for hiding it is not there
items.html: Part 0 says the organisation keeps people afraid "so that nobody persists." It never says what the organisation gains when nobody persists. The old man remembers across lives; other people scattering costs him nothing and gives him nothing in the plan. Anneke's reason (collapse, "killers and savages") is a reason for her to keep the secret after the vote, not a reason anyone started. "Every cycle costs them more" is the nearest thing to a motive and it is unexplained: costs what? You need one sentence of self-interest, for example: they can only come back into a world that still has their building, their names and their chair, so the world must not change faster than they can return to it. Kalder also needs a line here: he crossed, has no fear and no love, so what happens to him? Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 1.4 Nobody says what the review does or what the time is bought from
items.html: Part 0 promises James "buys the world time" and that the organisation is "preparing a small number of people to survive whatever comes next." But the review in v8.2 is records moved and eleven addresses visited. Then the bunkers turn out to be "fuel" and "the date passes and nothing loud happens." So there is no event to survive and nothing the world was about to lose. This reads like a reset that was cut from an earlier version while its consequences were left in. Either put a consequence back (what happens to a population when a review completes) or cut "buys the world time" and "whatever comes next" from the idea paragraph and let the stake be eleven addresses, which is honest and enough. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.5 Killing is not a rare failure in this plan
items.html: The List's rule is "correct → ridicule → buy → vanish. Killing is the failure mode," and the Deventer visitor says "a body's a fingerprint." Yet the plan shows a canal road in 1995, a canal in Zwolle, the professor in the blue chair, and "three were resolved this quarter" out of eleven addresses in one region. Three deaths a quarter per region is a routine. "Monday" even says they killed before "and it was cheap," which contradicts the fingerprint line. Decide which organisation this is. If killing is rare, make the three "resolved" addresses a care home, a bankruptcy and one death, and let the Zwolle canal be the exception people inside are uneasy about. That also makes Kalder the anomaly, which he should be. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.6 The numbers do not add up, top or bottom
items.html: "A few hundred professionals" must fill the right column, which only a handler who has crossed and stands close can judge. The payload shows 112 flagged people at one bank, and Kalder spends eight months of golf on one of them. A few hundred people cannot do that for the world. At the other end, "millions of helpers" are defeated by about two hundred sheets and one bank's board vote, and the old man retires. Is he the head of everything or of one Dutch foundation? The draft's "a generation, perhaps, in this part of the world" is the honest scale. Say in Part 0 that the book shows one regional node, and let "The math" do the handler arithmetic as well as the helper arithmetic. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.7 Erasing the job is the opposite of the method
items.html: "Leiden, 1931" states the method: leave the misprints, "a clean plate is a confession." In "The week it vanished" the organisation wipes a job from every backup going back years, "which should be impossible," and closes a ticket against one that never existed. That is the cleanest plate in the book and it tells James he is right. The same people leave the seat list findable. Also, the job is erased in Part One but "the job is gone in a month" at the end, and page 212 exists to hide a job that still runs. Make the Part One move a dirty one: the job is renamed, given an owner and a boring ticket, and only James's screenshot shows the difference. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.8 The machine hands James everything he beats it with, and never says why
items.html: Pieter puts him on the continuity programme ("they asked for the person who reads things"). From that role he reads the invoice, the seat annex and the field schedule with its Visit column. Bram even says "The wife will find the schedule. Let her." The seats are a decoy by design, but the invoice and the schedule are real evidence, and a machine built on nobody knowing anything keeps its hit list in a bank's programme files. The only reading that works is recruitment: "buy" comes before "vanish," and they are bringing him in. State that in a handler chapter, and give the schedule a reason to be where a new joiner can see it. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.9 The sheets promise "you are not on the list" to people who are on it
items.html: Part 0, truth three: James shows each helper "that they are not on the list." But Pieter, Anneke and the brewery man are on the seat list, and Pieter's sheet shows his children "per allocation." At the time of "The sheets" James still believes the seats are real; "the bunkers are fuel" comes four chapters later. So he cannot tell anyone the promise is empty, and the sheets work only on conscience (the three addresses). That is fine and probably better, but then truth three is wrong as written. Either move the fuel reveal to "What was on the phone," as a document, so the sheets can carry it, or rewrite truth three. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 1.10 The win works; the seats as a decoy and the thermostat work
items.html: Attacking the compartments with each person's own paperwork is the right ending for a monitoring engineer, and "nobody rises up. People just stop. And some don't" is the right scale. "Two hundred people hold their own names, and a body confirms every envelope" is a sound reason he lives. The seats "left findable" as the satisfying wrong answer is a good mechanism and matches "the bunkers are fuel." The heating half of the thermostat (grants in cold years) is well sourced and gives Frank's kitchen question an answer. Do not touch these. Severity: works.

items.title: 2.1 Anneke hears everything in December and is "turned" weeks later
items.html: She sits in the opening and in "The reading room, continued" while James lays out the invoice, the eleven addresses and three outcomes, and the old man offers five seats. In "The sheets" she reads her invoice and says "I'll need the rest of it," as if new to it. She is also "due to sign the quarter's schedule," which makes her a professional, not a helper. The v7 draft patches this with "You were in that room," but she still waited weeks after hearing about three deaths. Decide what she knew on the second of December and why she was in that chair. Simplest: the old man brought her to watch a recruitment, she had never seen the schedule, and that is the page that moves her. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 2.2 The dealer's phone call and "counted the night you asked" cannot both be true
items.html: In "Groningen" the dealer telephoned about James "three weeks ago, before the ticket." But the ticket is opened in "Leave it," and Groningen comes after three more weeks, the payload, the control case and the week it vanished. Three weeks before Groningen is after the ticket. Separately, Part 0 says writing to a dealer puts you in the left column, so James was counted when he wrote to the dealer, not "the night you asked" in stand-up, and the payload should already list him. Fix the order (dealer call first, and it is why Kalder turns up on the golf course in "A round with a stranger") and let the payload show two entries for him. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.3 The review date is moved four times and the last weeks do not fit
items.html: The date comes forward in "A car park," "Leiden, nine years ago," "The long table, again" and "The leak." It is the same beat each time. Part Two ends with "the review is two weeks away" on the second of December. Part Three then has the dinner, the phone, and "over three weeks James prepares" the sheets, before the review is "brought forward to Monday." Three weeks do not fit inside two, and a date already passed cannot be brought forward. Move it twice at most, and write one calendar from the second of December to the Monday. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.4 James leaves Buddy alone at an address he knows is listed for the dog
items.html: In "The schedule" he reads "companion" beside his own address, says "it's the dog," names the man from the pub, sends Ana and Mora away, and keeps the old dog in the house, "knowing a house with one old dog in it is a target." Eleven days later the dog is poisoned from a water bowl by the back gate. The man the whole book is built on would not do this, and readers forgive a hero almost anything except that. Give him a reason he cannot move Buddy (the stairs, the vet, a kennel that fails) or have him take precautions that Kalder beats. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 2.5 James knows who Kalder is long before "the nail," and does nothing with it
items.html: By "The money" he has read a seat contract that "runs through Kalder's consultancy." Then: Julian K. on the invoice, the invented book, "Deventer," the schedule. Each time the plan says "filed." Noor's identification in "The vet" is the seventh tell. The same habit recurs elsewhere: the four key-holders ("He says nothing"), and the depot reference format, which Noor explains in "Leiden" and which he then sees on a spine in "The drill" and "doesn't connect." A man who "checks everything" cannot file this much. Cut the tells to three, let him test one at work, and make Noor's call give him something new: the flask and Zwolle. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.6 The thin book is stolen for no reason, and the brief says it is not stolen
items.html: "Deventer, March" has the visitor photograph every page. So the organisation has the notebook, and Kalder has no need to poison a dog to take it. He also has no need to poison a dog to enter a house that stands empty every working day, and his own report says "the old dog is not a problem." The plan says the thin book is "gone" and photographs sit on the tablecloth; the v8 brief says it "is not stolen" and is on the tablecloth. Choose. The cleaner version: nothing is taken, the poisoning is the message, and it is Kalder's private act against the method. That is what "he fucked up with the dog" already says. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.7 Part Two is thirty-one chapters and James mostly reads paper in it
items.html: Thirteen of the thirty-one are not James in the present (interludes, villain, past). Of the rest, eight are "James finds a document": the folder, the generals' report, the invoice, page 212, the schedule, the other addresses, the accounts, the money shown to Frank. His first act that changes anything is the sheets, in Part Three. "The other ten," "The band" and "Frank, loose" sit together after the book's emotional peak and all add evidence the reader no longer needs. Fold "The band" into "Frank, loose," move "The other ten" before the floor night, and give James one thing to do in the middle that costs him. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.8 Part One ends on a summary and the climax happens without James
items.html: Part One's last chapter is "Groningen," a quiet conversation; the turn is in "The week it vanished," three chapters earlier. End the part there, or on the payload line with his number on it. Part Two ends well: he says no. Part Three's climax, the board vote, is "what happens elsewhere, imagined," while James putts. That is in character and the draft makes it funny, but it means the last thing he does on the page is deliver an envelope. Let Anneke's six a.m. doorstep carry more: one question from her that only he can answer. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.9 Ana and Kalder act from their own motives; Noor, Aylin and Frank less so
items.html: Ana refuses, leaves the address "not him," comes back, opens the door and improvises the pills: every step is hers. Kalder wants the seat, likes James, and acts for himself. Noor's rule is "never publish, never ask, always hide," yet she opens contact with a stranger on a forum the plan says is farmed; give her a reason that outweighs the rule. Aylin goes from proud keeper to propping the door at midnight on one question; she needs her own discovery in the visitor book. Frank is given a sheet although he was never a helper, and "honestly doesn't remember" a stand-up from the same week with no cause given. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.10 The ending in Part 0 is not the ending in the chapters, and James has a man removed
items.html: Part 0: the organisation "has to stop, re-think, and start again somewhere else." The chapters: the same foundation under Anneke, continuity stays, the truth stays hidden, James agrees to silence. Those are different books; the second is better and sadder, so rewrite the idea paragraph to match. Also, "Part of the deal was you gone" means James asked the organisation to hunt Kalder, and "the colleagues close in." A man who cannot pressure anyone has ordered something that looks like a killing, by the people whose killing he stopped. Decide what closing in means and whether James knows. PLACEHOLDER. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 2.11 Dates, counts and objects that disagree
items.html: The payload is forty kilobytes in the plan, forty-one in the brief. "Deventer" is said at the barbecue in the plan, at the pub in the brief. The last chapter is "Epilogue" in Part 1 and "Coda" plus an empty "Epilogue" in Part 2. The invoice is "billed per flagged person" yet steps only six times in thirty-one years while the list grows nightly. Corporate day calls Kalder "the stranger from the spring," but the books reach the market around June. The opening tray holds a "handwritten ledger" open "at page 118," which is the printed book's page. Kalder carries seven wedges and hits a driver: count to fourteen. The List still has about forty entries, coordinates on the last page, a date three weeks after the death, and entry 26 as a withdrawal, not "shared → coincident." Severity: small.

items.title: 3.1 The opening spends Part One's two discoveries
items.html: On page three the old man says the seats are findable and "you were counted the night you asked." Part One then builds to "The payload" (asking gets you counted) and ends on "the proof that his own bank counted him the night he asked." The reader has known since page three. The seats line costs nothing, because James misreads the seats until the end. The count line costs you the best turn in Part One. Keep the tray, the ledger, the silent woman, the seats and the generator in the opening; move "you were counted" to "The reading room, continued." This is your call. PLACEHOLDER. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 3.2 The appointment that drives Part One has no payoff
items.html: The thin book ends on a reference number, the second of December and the word Ask. Noor says "nobody has ever simply asked for it." Then James arrives, the tray is already out, and the scene becomes the old man's offer. He never asks, never reads the item, and decision 1 ("the one deleted sentence James reads on the second of December") has no beat in either reading-room chapter. Aylin's "Not today, but we were expecting you" also makes it unclear whose appointment it was, and why a man who died in March was booked for December. Put the asking and the reading on the page; it is the object the whole book has been walking toward. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 3.3 "Some of us remember" is not news when the old man says it
items.html: In "The night he stops being afraid" James sees lives, "short and ordinary and cut off by somebody's administration," and a hand he has "seen all his life." He has remembered. The reader has known since "Leiden, nine years ago" that crossing is real. So item six of the final conversation, delivered "lightly," confirms what both already have. What is new is only that the top does it on purpose, with a method, to stay. Lead with that. The callback ("it's not for staying") is the real reveal in the scene and it is James's; the plan should say so and cut the build-up to the old man's line. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 3.4 Part 0 promises a religion layer that has no chapter
