items.html: "Where every reveal goes" lists, for Part Two, "through Noor, the shelf and Beard Man": the knowledge-bringers punished, the old gods rewritten as demons, "the warden who calls himself God," "within" turned into "through us," the names as passwords, the window the size of a meal. No Part Two chapter summary contains any of it. Two items appear as PLACEHOLDER topics under "Leiden." Beard Man does not appear after "The week it vanished." The warden is never paid off: the top turns out to be people. "Frank, loose" adds a third cosmology (a simulation that renders what is observed) beside the pool and the warden. Choose the pool, give Beard Man a second scene, and cut the warden or say who he is. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 3.5 Things set up and not paid off
items.html: "The original has a hand in it": who gave is never answered (see 6.3). "That night James starts building something … and doesn't describe it": never named. The visitor book is shown, copied at midnight and delivered, but the plan never says what it proves. "The hearings on the bar TV" are laid on the table in December with no earlier scene. The edited forum persona, the gorilla fitted to James himself, is seen by eleven people and costs him nothing with Ana, Frank or work. The shelf of novels is "paid off later" only by a line about VALIS; Blindsight argues against the book's own thesis and nobody notices. The Dalai Lama search is "confirmed" without ever having been raised. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 3.6 The reader's knowledge of Kalder is well ordered; the small objects pay off
items.html: "Leiden, nine years ago" names Kalder and his crossing before "On land," so the pub and barbecue play as dread, not puzzle. That is the right choice, and it settles decision 4: the car park chapter can stay anonymous or go, because two chapters later the reader is told anyway. The flask (Zwolle, Noor, the widow's photograph), the invented book (pub to dinner), the bag by the door (dinner to market) and the promise to run (kitchen floor to dinner) are each planted once and used once. Leave them alone. Severity: works.

items.title: 4.1 Down House, 1860: the dates and the "pressure" need checking
items.html: Darwin did add "by the Creator" to the last sentence in the second edition, and the regret letter is real (to Hooker, 29 March 1863: he had "truckled to public opinion"). Check this: the second edition was corrected in late 1859, partly at Ilkley, and published 7 January 1860, weeks after the first, so "1860, at his desk" and "under public pressure" may both be off. The 1863 letter is about using the word "creation," not expressly those three words. Check where the letter is held (Cambridge University Library, I believe). Note also that Darwin added a hand and the organisation removes them; let James say that, or the chapter argues the wrong way. Severity: small.

items.title: 4.2 Croton, 530 BC: the source is a joke told against Pythagoras
items.html: The dog story survives as a few lines by Xenophanes, a contemporary, quoted centuries later by Diogenes Laertius, and it is usually read as mockery. It gives no place and no year; Croton and 530 BC are when Pythagoras is thought to have moved there. The brief's rule for interludes is "real people doing documented things only." So tell it as what it is: a rival's verse, the first surviving mention of the idea, already wearing a gorilla mask in the sixth century BC. That fits the book better than a straight scene and keeps you inside the rule. Check this against a translation before quoting. Severity: small.

items.title: 4.3 Mexico City, 1994: accurate, but its placement accuses
items.html: Jacobo Grinberg did vanish in December 1994 and his "transferred potential" experiments used pairs in separate shielded rooms. Check this: the result has not been solidly replicated, and the brief wants that said. The problem is position. "Utrecht, 1993" invents a Dutch replication, the foundation calls it "recall," the author dies on a canal road, and entry 26 notes "same method." Then comes the real disappearance, "facts only." The reader will conclude your organisation took a real man whose family is alive. That is an invented act attached to a real person, which the rule forbids in spirit. Add one sentence of the narrator refusing the inference, or move the interlude away from "Leiden." Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 4.4 Washington, 1953: not a weekend, and not proof the policy ran
items.html: Check this: the Robertson Panel met 14 to 17 January 1953, Wednesday to Saturday, and one of the five arrived late. "Five scientists, one weekend" looks wrong. The recommendation to debunk through mass media, with Disney named, is in the Durant report; quote from the report itself, not from a secondary book, and confirm the "burden of proof" wording is there. "Frank's kitchen" then has James read it as "a standard of proof that was taught until nobody remembered it was taught." The record supports a recommendation; whether the education program was carried out is disputed. Let Frank say that, since it is exactly his objection, and let "the memo's the table" stand as the draw. Severity: small.

items.title: 4.5 Urfa, 1994: sound, with one loose number
items.html: Klaus Schmidt did visit Göbekli Tepe in 1994, the name does mean Potbelly Hill, and it lies about fifteen kilometres from Urfa, so Tresidder walking out of the town in 1929 fits. Check this: the site was noted in a 1963 survey and dismissed, which is a gift you are not using, and the direction is northeast. "The date of civilisation moves by six thousand years" is the popular comparison with Stonehenge, not a finding; say what moved (monumental building before farming). "The book never says he found it" is the right restraint. Severity: works.

items.title: 4.6 The 1999 French report is not quite what "Leiden" says it is
items.html: COMETA was a private association's report, published in a magazine, by a committee chaired by an air force general with other senior officers and engineers; it was not an official government document and its authors were not all generals. Check this: the passage about sacred texts, films and "suitable sects" is in the political chapter, not the last chapter, and it is a thought experiment about how visitors might handle us. "Its authors feared only being seen up close" is the MindBook's reading, tagged probable there. Noor is a conservator and would be exact: have her say "a private report by retired officers" and read the passage as a thought experiment. It still works on James. Severity: small.

items.title: 4.7 "Every book" breaks the rule against invented edits on real books
items.html: The rule: "no invented edit attached to a real book." But the old man says they took one thing "out of every book in the world," Part 0 says "every book that said knowledge was given now says it arose," and the religion layer has "within" turned into "through us," which any reader will hear as the Gospels. A universal claim lands on real books by definition, and the narration half-confirms it through James's floor night. Keep the forty-one as the only edits the book asserts. Make "every book" visibly the old man's boast, and present "within / through us" as a known translation and doctrine dispute that Noor points at, not as an edit. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 4.8 The final conversation names real films, a real studio founder and a living institution
items.html: The brief allows real works "only as the old man's claims," and the draft keeps to that. Three still carry risk. "I Origins was made to discredit a good theory" says living filmmakers were instruments. "Walt was our best customer" names a man whose company exists. The Dalai Lama search "confirmed" as cover is a claim about a living religious tradition and a living person. Check this: Dick's 1974 experience, his son's diagnosis and the eight years of writing are roughly as stated, but he was trying to explain it, not disprove it. Keep the list short, keep James laughing at it, and consider cutting I Origins to "a small film about eyes." Severity: small.

items.title: 4.9 The List breaks the rule in one entry and is out of date
items.html: Entry 31 puts an invented log transcript and an invented memo ("handled with humor") on the real P-59 program and three pilots. The MindBook brief says the gorilla-mask anecdote has no primary document and "the narration should not assert it." Frank telling it as a story is fine; the List entry is an invented edit on a real record. Entry 7 dates a water-erosion paper to 1979; the real hypothesis in geology is from the early 1990s, so an invented 1979 paper predates the idea it leans on. Check this. Entries 14, 17, 22, 34 and 38 are safely invented and well made. Bring the List into line with v8.2 before anyone drafts from it. Severity: small.

items.title: 5.1 The biggest document in the book is taken by force
items.html: The rules: James "cannot access sealed archives by stealth, pressure institutions, or 'hack' anything," and a door opens only when "someone chooses to open it." In "The dinner" Kalder is drugged and "they unlock his phone with his thumb." Everything in "What was on the phone" (handlers, schedule, allocations, the tier list that makes the sheets possible) comes from that. Ana's pills are a great beat and hers to do. The thumb is the breach. Alternatives that keep the rule: Kalder leaves the phone behind on purpose because he likes James and is loyal only to himself; or the photographs of him asleep are the whole prize and the tier list comes from Pieter or Aylin, who choose. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 5.2 The truth arrives as a speech, twice
items.html: The rule: "Reveals arrive as objects in James's hands, never as speeches." "The final conversation" is planned as nine items from the old man with "nothing on the table." The draft breaks it up well and has James doubt it, but the central truth of the novel is still something a villain says. "Compartments" is 1,500 words of "the understanding, said plainly," with no scene, and it repeats "The math" and the phone list. Give the final conversation one object, the page James asked for in December, and let the old man talk around it. Fold "Compartments" into "What was on the phone" as a paragraph. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 5.3 The dog rule is broken by the organisation's tables, and that could be the point
items.html: "Every chapter with a table has a dog under it." No dog is planned in "A room with a long table," "The long table, again," "Deventer, March," "Washington, 1953," either reading-room chapter, "Frank's kitchen" or "Leiden." The v8 draft of "The final conversation" turns the lack into a line: "There was no dog under the table. First table in a year." That is the better rule: every table James sits at has a dog, and the organisation's tables never do, which is "companion animals are not accommodated" made visible. Write it that way in Part 0, and put Buddy in Frank's kitchen and Noor's. Severity: small.

items.title: 5.4 Part Three has no jokes in the plan
items.html: "The book stays funny to the end" is a rule, and Parts One and Two have their comedy built into the beats: the toaster story, the hat sizes, the gorilla mask, Beard Man. From "What was on the phone" to "The leak" the beats are understanding, delivery and threat, with no comic object named. The drafts find some (Walt, "I'm not your secretary"), which shows it can be done, but a plan that does not name the joke loses it in revision. Name one per chapter in the beats. Beard Man is the obvious missing instrument: he has not been seen since Part One and he owes the book a second theory. Severity: small.

items.title: 5.5 The doors that open do open by choice
items.html: Els rings back because of one line. The Groningen dealer stops telephoning after one question. Noor refuses to be a witness and gives a shelfmark instead. Aylin shows the visitor book and props the door. Pieter asks what to do and is told "nothing." James reads only what his new role lets him read, and the payload capture is inside his own job. Outside the dinner, the rule holds through the whole plan, and it is what makes James different from every other conspiracy hero. Keep "Twenty minutes" exactly as planned: objects on a tablecloth, six "I don't know"s, "I believe you." Severity: works.

items.title: 6.1 What is the sentence?
items.html: Decision 1, "the one deleted sentence James reads on the second of December," is the object the book exists to deliver. Everything in 1.1, 1.2 and 3.2 waits on it. It has to be an instruction a reader could use, short enough to remember, plain enough to have sat unnoticed in a dry book, and connected to "given." It should not be attached to any real text. Until you write it, nobody can draft either reading-room chapter or the epilogue honestly. PLACEHOLDER. Severity: breaks the story.

items.title: 6.2 At the end, does James meet Buddy or does Buddy come back?
items.html: The plan runs two models. One is a cycle: people scatter into a pool or return, and remembering lets you leave. The other is a meeting: "He's in a better place. I'll see him soon." Then Ida sits at the stairs "the way only Buddy did," which suggests return, although the old man says nobody knows where the door goes. The draft's answer is that James "can't check this one," which is honest, but the reader needs to know which hope he holds. Ana's belief about her grandmother is "never proved wrong"; is James's ever proved right? PLACEHOLDER. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 6.3 Who gave?
items.html: "The sentence" ends on "the original has a hand in it," and the edits remove that hand forty-one times. Part Two's notes point at knowledge-bringers and old gods. The final conversation says only that some people remember. Is the hand those people, in earlier lives? Something else the book declines to name? Nothing at all? The MindBook brief warns that if the top is non-human the book becomes someone else's. If you mean to leave it open, say so in Part 0 so that drafts do not answer it by accident. PLACEHOLDER. Severity: weakens it.

items.title: 6.4 What does the organisation want, in one sentence it would say to itself?
items.html: Not Anneke's reason and not the cover told to helpers: the old man's own. Findings 1.3 and 1.4 cannot be fixed without it. Related: is the old man the top, or one regional head who believes he is the top? The MindBook's best find ("the same name covers a vassal and his suzerain") is not used anywhere in v8.2 and would answer the scale problem in 1.6 for free. PLACEHOLDER. Severity: breaks the story.

reviews.title: Review 02 — the engine proposals, tested
reviews.intro:
15 Nov 2026. Read in full: THE BOOK v8.2, the v8 brief, ADDENDUM 05, the Engines README, section 5 of all ten maps, section 4 of the King and Illuminatus! maps, v7 The money. Searched for specific lines: v7 The drill, The other ten, Frank, loose, The reading room, continued, The sheets, The leak, The corporate day; v6 On land, The math, A car park, The gorilla mask, The vet, Twenty minutes.

One of the three ranked changes survives close to how it is written, one survives if you point it at a different action, and one survives only as a single object. Change 1 (The money) is the right first move, but its central detail is a misreading: Pieter's three dependants are his wife and two children, so there is nothing to correct. Change 2 (the gate) forbids James from handing out sheets twenty chapters before he has the idea of a sheet, and its timetable needs about seven weeks between a night in November and the second of December. Change 3 (the referral) is one more document handed to James, the thing he chooses is to stop, and the chain from his cover to the poisoned dog breaks on the calendar.

The table has a wider problem. The diagnosis in PIPELINE.md names two chapters (The drill, The money). The table changes fifteen of thirty-one rows, including fourteen of James's eighteen chapters, and removes nothing. With everything in, James puts his name on their paper five times, and the old man reads five things back to him in a scene your plan says he spends refusing specifics. Your plan already has two acts with a price (he lets Ana leave and the house becomes a target; he goes to Noor and she is made quiet). The passive stretch is The math through Enjoy it while it lasts, and that is where the work belongs.

The order I would do them in: first the request slip in The reading room, continued (two lines, and it pays the thin book's Ask). Second, The money as a reconciliation whose result is the names that are in the annex and absent from HR. Third, the gate, with one condition, aimed at warning the people on the schedule. Last, the referral as a form James signs and the old man reads back, with no counselor, no card for Ana and no link to the date. Drop the carrier errand in The drill, the shelfmark hook in On land, the hair on the thin book, Buddy at Frank's flat, the film in The band and the access review in Enjoy it while it lasts.

items.title: 1.1 The annex is right, so James has nothing to correct
items.html: Change 1 has James "correct Pieter's three dependants to two." v7 The money says "Dependants per allocation: 3. He has two children," and the addendum reads that as an error in the annex. v7 The sheets resolves it: "Two kids. Lotte and Bas. And Marieke. That's three." v7 The leak repeats it: "She's one of my three." HR records would show the same three. If James makes the correction, he strikes Pieter's wife off the seat list, and Rose 5.2 (a fourth place for the mother) and Illuminatus! 5.3 ("his three dependants") both stop adding up. Keep the task. Replace the result (1.2). Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.2 What the reconciliation would really find is the names with no HR record
items.html: Part 0 says the organization "hides its own seats inside that contract," and The money already puts a brewery executive on the bank's annex. A reconciliation against HR turns up exactly those names. That is the result to give James: a short list of people on Annex C who do not work at the bank. He takes it to Pieter. Pieter says they are vendor allocations and to sign. James signs. That is a second "leave it," it is a choice, and his initials now cover the hidden seats specifically. The old man's thanks in The reading room, continued then has a point. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.3 The side effects in The money and Enjoy it while it lasts contradict each other
items.html: The money row says the role "came through already ticked," so Saskia did not grant it. The next row has Saskia lose her right to grant roles because she "can't say who granted it." The same row has James write "the dull true reason" and leave "the annex out," but under change 1 the annex reconciliation is his assigned task with his initials on it, so there is nothing to leave out. Enjoy it while it lasts already holds page 212, the review date, the narrowed access, Kalder's tip and Julian K. Keep "already ticked" as one line in The money. Drop the access review and Saskia's move. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 1.4 He initials before he reads the small type, and the cost waits for Part Three
items.html: The row has James sign off the annex and "only then" read companion animals are not accommodated. v7 The money has him say "I don't skim. I can't." He would read the terms first. Let him read the line, think of Buddy in the car, and sign anyway, because Pieter is waiting. Also fix the order inside the chapter: he signs the annex first and finds the foundation's invoice line after, so he learns what he signed one evening too late. As written, nothing goes wrong inside Part Two; the old man's thanks in The reading room, continued is the only Part Two payoff, so it must stay. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.5 The gate forbids sheets twenty chapters before James thinks of a sheet
items.html: The Leiden row has James write "no sheet to anyone until Frank has tried to explain one piece of paper and failed." In v8.2 the sheet is invented in Compartments and The sheets, after Kalder's phone. In v7 the idea first appears as the last line of The other ten ("And then I'm going to tell them"). In Leiden James has no plan to give anyone anything, so the rule holds back nothing and the "schedule dates that pass while he waits" are not its cost. Aim the gate at the one thing he can do in Part Two once he holds the schedule: warn the people at the other addresses. Write the rule in The schedule or Twenty minutes. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.6 The gate has two conditions, and James breaks it twice without the table noticing
items.html: Leiden's row says Frank opens it. The other ten's row says the eighth address is "the test he must witness before anyone gets a sheet." Section c says "tested at the eighth address, opened in Frank, loose," which is two gates with one name. Between them James tells Ana the truth in The schedule, goes to Leiden "to make Noor a witness" in The vet, and lays everything out in Twenty minutes. A gate that allows all three binds nothing. Pick Frank as the only condition, and say what the gate does not cover: Ana. Move the Noor attempt so that it is the reason he writes the rule. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.7 The choice at the eighth address is false, because they gave him the schedule
items.html: The row says knocking "tells the organization he holds the schedule." In A room with a long table Bram says "The wife will find the schedule. Let her." They know he has it. The real price of a warning is in your own machine: a person who is told starts asking, and everyone who asks is counted, as in Groningen. Use that. For the PLACEHOLDER, choose "quiet" or "moved." If the eighth address ends dead after James watched from a car, he traded a life for a test, the book has to carry that to the end, and "kills rarely" stops being true. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.8 "Pulled" and "handed" do not sort the way the table says
items.html: Twenty minutes' row says "nearly every route runs through the program or Julian." The edits, the thin book, the payload he captured, his screenshot, Groningen, Els's folder and Noor all came before the program or outside it. And the invoices Frank is shown as "pulled" were queried through the role that "came through already ticked." Narrow the question to the one thing the reader knows was bait: the schedule. The other ten checks it against public records. For Frank, let The band do the work: the foundation's published accounts show the same steps as the invoice. Then "I believe the invoice" rests on paper nobody gave him. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.9 The gate's timetable does not fit before the second of December
items.html: v7 The reading room, continued dates the poisoning "a night in November." After it the table needs: Noor's visit and the van, four nights on the floor, Twenty minutes, Ana "home a week" (v7 Frank, loose), an eighth date "nine days off," the address going quiet "a week later," a weekend on the wrong film, and Frank's line "you saw your own book in the accounts last month." That is about seven weeks, and the ninth date still has to pass. The addendum admits to losing one week. Either the poisoning moves to early October, which pulls The schedule and the barbecue with it, or the eighth-address watch and the "last month" line go. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.10 The referral is one more paper handed to James, and what he chooses is to stop
items.html: Change 3 is sold as "the switch to 'he chose' in the third James chapter." Pieter hands him a form someone else filled in; that is receiving. What he then chooses is to go quiet, and in v8.2 The math he already "withdraws from everyone." So the change adds a cover for an inaction the plan has. It also contradicts its neighbors: the row has him "stop asking at work," and the money row then has him ask Saskia who granted his role. The form itself is good: it shows him that the bank knows about his books, it is funny, and it uses the rule Els's folder prints. Keep the form. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 1.11 The chain from cover to date to dog breaks in three places
items.html: First, A car park is eleven chapters before The schedule, so the date James reads there was printed after the move; it cannot then be "wrong about the date" because of that move. Second, in v6 A car park the date moves because Kalder shades his report ("You brought it forward, not me"), which is a Kalder beat the rewrite gives away. Third, the row says James "finds out in The vet"; he has no paper there that shows why a date moved. He could learn it only from the phone in Part Three. The row also leans on your undecided question 4 (keep, cut or identify the car park). Drop the chain. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 1.12 The "one discredit slot" is already taken, and the referral costs three scenes
items.html: The addendum says the folder's rule is printed and "nothing on the page uses it." The gorilla mask uses it: James's forum persona is edited "with bloodlines," and the King map lists that as on the page. So the referral is a second reclassification. It can work as the office twin of the forum one if it stays small. As written it needs a one-to-one, at least one counselor session and Ana finding the card, in what is already the longest chapter of the movement; the counselor is a new helper who then needs a sheet; and the card erases the breakfast where Ana "catches the join." Cut it to the form, the signature, and the old man reading it back. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 2.1 With everything in, James puts his name on their paper five times
items.html: The referral (The math), the visitor book (The drill), the annex (The money), the access-review reason (Enjoy it while it lasts) and the request slip (The reading room, continued). The stated cost of each is the same: his name in their file. Four of the five come to him through Pieter, who hands him the referral, sends him upstairs, tells him to sign and countersigns the reason, so your unknowing helper starts to look like the organization's arm. Keep two signatures: the annex, which makes him a helper, and the slip, which is the first thing he asks for. The referral can be a third only if it is over in half a page. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 2.2 The reading room, continued receives five readbacks
items.html: If all rows go in, the old man thanks James for the annex, reads the referral back, says nobody came to the eighth address because James was there, uses the fact that the strongest papers are theirs, and reads the request slip "upside down." Ana already reads the schedule upside down in The schedule. v8.2 says the old man "refuses every specific" and has six findings, the offer, the refusal and the lower door in about three thousand words. Choose two readbacks. I would take the thanks for the annex, because it is the cost of change 1, and "He asked too." Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 2.3 Part Two with all three in, chapter by chapter
items.html: The math: folder, then referral; he goes quiet. Leiden: a rule about sheets. The drill: carries an envelope, signs. The money: asks, reconciles, signs. Enjoy it while it lasts: writes a reason. On land: a trap with a shelfmark. The gorilla mask: a hair. The schedule: books the dog a room. The vet: checks the hair. Twenty minutes: labels sources. The other ten: watches a street. The band: wrong for a weekend. Frank, loose: sorts two piles. The reading room, continued: files a slip. That is a man doing paperwork about paperwork in fourteen chapters. The first movement (The math to Enjoy it while it lasts) holds as one story with changes 1 and a small 3. The third movement holds with one gate. The middle needs none of it. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 3.1 The drill: the errand opens a door your plan keeps shut and shows James too much
items.html: v8.2 has "a glass door he isn't badged for." The row has Aylin buzz him through, which removes one of the few closed doors in Part Two. He signs "the bound book on her desk," and the man who reads everything would read the lines above his own, where v7 The sheets puts the professor in March with the shelfmark and Deceased. That spends The sheets' reveal. A bank envelope going to the foundation's desk also hands him the link he is meant to find in The money. And he is sent, which is still receiving. Leave the glass door shut. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 3.2 On land: the hook fails, and the club weekend rehearses the ending
items.html: Nobody says a shelfmark aloud in a pub during a toaster story. If James says one in the depot's format, he tells Kalder he knows the depot. The organization would check its own catalog, find nothing and know it was bait; it has no reason to ask a book dealer about a depot shelfmark. A readout through Groningen also confirms Kalder weeks before The vet, where v8.2 says "This is the nail." The "no dogs, sorry" weekend spends the five-seats refusal early, and Kalder asked about Buddy before he asked James's name, so no single sentence put "companion" on the schedule. Keep the plan's version: a word, a trap, a nod. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 3.3 The gorilla mask: the Buddy test is redundant and the hair is spy tradecraft
items.html: The row has James agree to the barbecue "to see what Buddy does with Kalder in the house." Buddy rides in the cart (v7 The corporate day: "Bring the old boy"), so James has watched the two of them for months. The brief's kill list has "heist competence"; a hair across a book is that. The cost in the row is worth keeping without the motive: Kalder learns the back lane, the fourth gate and the bowl at a barbecue James agreed to. The four-in-the-morning build should stay something an engineer builds (5.2). Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 3.4 The schedule: sending Buddy to Frank's flat makes Frank's address the target
items.html: v8.2's reason for Ana leaving is that the alternative is "her name on a list," and the note on the schedule is "companion." By the plan's own logic the visit follows the dog. Booking Buddy into Frank's flat puts Frank, who is "never in it," on the schedule, and James would see that. The brief also says Buddy "can't do the stairs," and v6 Frank's kitchen has Frank walk James down the stairs. The useful half of King 2 is already in your plan: James lets Ana and Mora go "knowing a house with one old dog in it is a target." Let him say that he chose it. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 3.5 The vet: an untouched hair cannot tell him the book was photographed
items.html: The row says the hair is "exactly where he left it: photographed, not taken." An undisturbed hair shows nothing was touched. In Orwell the hero learns the dust was replaced only under interrogation; James has no such source. Deventer, March also has the visitor photograph "every page while the professor sleeps," so the organization has held the contents since March and has no reason to enter the house for pictures. The second half of the row is sound: James rings Noor's workshop and a colleague answers. Place it after Leiden, Friday so that the reader sees the afternoon before James hears its result. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 3.6 The band: the wrong film undoes the trap in On land
items.html: The row has James find "his own invented title" in the grant list and learn it is "a real, unrelated film with a near title." Published accounts list past years, so a grant cannot answer a title he invented weeks ago, and James reads dates. Worse, if a real film has nearly that title, Kalder's "Oh, that one. Yes" has an innocent reading, and The dinner's "the book you said you'd read" loses its force. Give The band a cheaper negative with no invention: one cold year with no grant, or one grant in a hot year. James cannot explain it and Frank finds it. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 3.7 The reading room, continued: the request is right; the placement and the payoff need care
items.html: No plan or draft has James ask for the shelfmark, and v7 The sheets says "No shelfmark; I hadn't asked for one." The row places it "on the way out," where it competes with the lower door, and has the old man "passing" a desk he is not at. Put the slip on the table before the offer, so the old man reads it where he sits. The payoff in The final conversation ("brings the item") also touches your decision 1, the deleted sentence James reads on the second of December. Decide what the tray shows and what the slip fetches before drafting either scene. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 3.8 The other rows
items.html: Sound as written: Deventer, March; Croton, 530 BC; Frank's kitchen; The corporate day; Mexico City, 1994; A room with a long table; Leiden, nine years ago; The promise; A street, night; Leiden, Friday; A corridor, sixteen; The night he stops being afraid; Urfa, 1994; The long table, again; Leiden, 1931. Two small problems. The Washington, 1953 row notes that Frank's kitchen already gives the reader the panel and proposes nothing; give Frank the quoted sentence and the interlude the room. Leiden's optional comparison has James show Els's private papers to a stranger soon after she trusted him, for a one-line difference nobody has chosen. Drop that option. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 4.1 A, the gate: the verdict holds, but the Walker test only works with a fixed future
items.html: In King the hero knows the date and the outcome of the test because he comes from later; the King map says "the calendar is what makes waiting forced." James's calendar is the schedule, which the organization wrote and can change, so they can answer any test by staying home. The table has them do exactly that. A watched address can never open James's gate. Only a person can, and the addendum does say so ("a person (Frank) chooses to open it"). The "rival reader as the clock" from Rose is stretched: in that book the rival is a man on stage who convicts people, and SDF's "plausible endings" have no such face. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 4.2 B, the canary: the verdict and the ranking disagree
items.html: Section a says to give the On land invention "Eco's four parts." Section c drops the same canary to fourth because "a canary needs no invention." Eco's version works because his believers want the invented thing to be true and act on it; Kalder is a professional with a catalog, so the most he does is nod. The plan's small version already fits that. The "one true public sentence" from Rose needs a closed place where every listener is a suspect. James has had his: stand-up in Leave it, read back in The payload as "asked (job)." B is already Part One's engine. Build nothing. Verdict: works.

items.title: 4.3 C, the front: neither change meets the condition the verdict rests on
items.html: The Illuminatus! map's first condition is that someone "acts on a layer as if it were the bottom" and pays. In its example the man believes the kind version and defends the conspiracy. Wearing the referral is the opposite: James knows it is a cover. Signing the annex is duty. The one proposal that meets the condition is the runner-up in The math's row, the Deventer neighbor whose version James believes and carries to Els. Calling The night he stops being afraid the "floor" is also stretched, because the seats layer breaks only in The final conversation. If you want C, take the neighbor. It also gives Els's refusal a cause. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 4.4 D, lock and key: "nothing to build" rests on a line that is not written
items.html: The verdict lists "Els's line" as on the page. In v8.2 it is "one thing (still to be chosen)," your decision 5. That line is the only key in Part Two that James has to find himself. The other locks open without him: Noor writes first, the role arrives ticked, and the narrowed access in Enjoy it while it lasts is fixed in eleven minutes on Kalder's tip. The README's problem statement has two halves, and "nothing blocks him" is a D problem. The addendum answers the other half and leaves this one. See 5.3. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 5.1 Your plan already has two acts that cost someone, and the addendum's premise skips them
items.html: The addendum says "nothing he does can go wrong except by frightening him." In The schedule James lets Ana and Mora go "knowing a house with one old dog in it is a target," and A street, night follows. In The vet he goes to Leiden to make Noor a witness, and Leiden, Friday follows. Both are choices, and both are paid by somebody else. What is missing is James saying so. One sentence in The vet about the empty house and the phone call to Noor's workshop do more for the middle of Part Two than the six rows aimed at it. Verdict: works.

items.title: 5.2 James never uses his trade in Part Two
items.html: In The payload he captures forty kilobytes because that is what an engineer does. After that he reads. The gorilla mask has him "building something at four in the morning" that the plan never describes, and the addendum turns it into a hair. Let him build what he builds at work: a monitor, on public sources only. Death notices, the land registry and the company register for the eleven addresses, checked every night at fourteen minutes past two. Then The other ten is his own alert going off, and what he checks the handed schedule against is something he made. Part Three is called The Instrument. No rule is broken: nothing is hacked. Verdict: works.

items.title: 5.3 No row puts a closed door in front of James
items.html: Fifteen rows change and not one of them stops him; the drill row opens a door the plan had shut. The cheap fixes are in the plan. Leave the glass door shut until December. Let the narrowed access in Enjoy it while it lasts stay narrowed for a chapter before Kalder's tip, so that taking the tip costs James something he can feel. Let Els's refusal stand for longer than "a week later Els rings," with the line he said doing its work offstage. A block the reader can see does what the gate tries to do with a written rule. Verdict: works.

items.title: 5.4 James never tries the winning move too early and fails
items.html: He wins by telling helpers what they did. Groningen is the accident that shows it works. In Part Two he never tries it on purpose. Let him try once, before the phone, on a helper whose "small believable reason" he has to guess. The site manager or Saskia would serve. He guesses wrong, the person hears a crank, and it goes in a file. That is an act that goes wrong for a reason other than fear, and it explains why the list on Kalder's phone ("what each helper had been told, by tier") is the thing he needed. The gate, re-aimed as in 1.5, is the rule he writes afterward. Verdict: works.

sections.title: 6. The canon conflicts, with a recommendation each

items.title: 6.1 The thin book, stolen or not
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Stolen. v8.2 The vet says "the thin book gone" and Twenty minutes has "photographs where the thin book should be"; v7 The reading room, continued puts it on the old man's tray. Only the brief and v6 keep it in the kitchen, and the brief's own first line says v8.2 wins. Deventer, March settles the logic: they photographed every page in March, so the only reason to enter the house is the original. Taking it leaves James with pictures, which is discredit. Cheapest fix: change one sentence in the brief, and drop the hair. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.2 Where "Deventer" is said
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. The barbecue, as the addendum says. v8.2 The gorilla mask has it ("says 'Deventer,' a town James has never written down; filed"), and v8.2 On land already carries the obscure word and the invented book. In v6 the Deventer slip ends the friendship on the spot, which On land must not do. Amend the brief's "Deventer slip" paragraph to the barbecue. Reuse the body passage from v6 On land ("a single hard knock") there. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.3 Lurker or twelve years of posts
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Both can stand. For twelve years he posted safe did-you-knows (v6 The gorilla mask: "every steam engine, every calendar") and never once asked a question of his own. "What I'd never done was speak" in your chapter can mean that without a word changed. The edit in The gorilla mask needs a persona to edit, and the count needs the difference between posting and asking. Fix the outlier, v6 A car park: "He deleted the one post he ever wrote" becomes the one question. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.4 What the invoice step is tied to
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. The asking, dated in the ticket week. v7 The money dates the step "the Monday of the week I opened my ticket" and the ticket to "a Thursday afternoon," so the step comes three days before the ticket. What preceded it is stand-up and the payload line "asked (job)," which matches the opening's "counted the night you asked." One sentence fixes it: counted the night he asked, billed the following Monday. The forum version in v8 Leave it cannot stand, because he deleted that question unposted, and a machine that logs unposted text is a different book. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 6.5 On land exists only in the plan
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Write it new from v8.2: the pub, the toaster story, the word, the invented book, "Oh, that one. Yes," and the friendship continuing. Leave out the year, the shelfmark and the club weekend (3.2). The chapter's job in the plan is that James is "not sure it was even a slip" and must carry that through the barbecue. From v6 keep Ana's toaster story and nothing after the slip. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.6 James never asks for the shelfmark
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Put the request in The reading room, continued, on the table, before the offer (3.7). The opening is on page three, where the reader does not yet know the word Ask, so the slip would mean nothing there. The final conversation should hold the answer, with the question already asked. This is the cheapest change in the addendum and the only one with no downstream damage. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.7 Noor's "nobody has ever simply asked" against the professor's March line
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Keep both with the bridge. v8.2 Deventer, March has the professor write "to the organisation's post box asking someone to come and talk." He never stood at the desk. v6 The vet already separates the two ("Because you asked instead of argued"). So the March line in the visitor book is Aylin entering a letter that named the shelfmark and booked the second of December. Noor's sentence stays true if she means in person and without an argument. The cost is one clause in her line. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.8 The brewery man on or off the seat list
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. On it. v8.2 The money, v8.2 The sheets and the brief agree: five seats, "I'm in." v7 The sheets is the only source that takes him off, and it loses the best refusal in the chapter. Being on the bank's annex without working at the bank also makes him the natural result of the reconciliation in 1.2. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.9 Which ticket closes the book
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. One ticket, against page 212, filed with Frank in Leave it, as v8.2 has it. It pays the Epilogue's "Page 212 is gone." James cannot file against rcl-agg: The week it vanished removed the job "from the list and from every backup," so he has nothing to point at. Anneke can report the job gone. Cut the v7 The sheets ticket "as a test," and do not add Libra 5.4, which puts Frank on the nightly list. Verdict: keep.

items.title: 6.10 Nine years, three times
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Two of the three are one event: Kalder crossed in Noor's kitchen nine years ago, so she has not seen him for nine years. Aylin's nine years at the desk is the stray. A reader will take three nines as a clue. Make it one with a single line: the Leiden transfer Kalder oversaw is what brought the collection to the depot and the desk its keeper. That gives Aylin's sheet a date without Rose 5.1's Thursdays. If you do not want the link, change her number. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 6.11 A dead man among the quiet four
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Henk drowned, so Zwolle is a resolved address. Count it as one of the three resolved ("each plausibly" covers a canal) and keep the quiet four living, which also lets one of them be met later. Move v7's first resolved address out of Deventer; the professor's house and the neighbor are enough for one town. Two small edits when The other ten is redrafted. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 6.12 Their date in December
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Their date has passed by the second of December: The schedule puts it eleven days off, and v6 The vet says "the date was yesterday." Change v7's "three dates still on it, and one of them was ours" so that their line is a past date with nothing written against it, because Buddy lived. The clock at the end of Part Two is the review, "two weeks away," as v8.2 says. Verdict: keep, changed.

items.title: 6.13 Ana suspects Julian before she likes him
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Cut the suspicion, and most of the scene with it. v8.2 The money ends with James alone: "He closes it and goes to get Buddy from the car." Part 0 says he "tells her everything once," and that is Twenty minutes. In v7 The money she reads the annex over his shoulder, which spends The schedule and Twenty minutes early, and her "unless it's their job" makes "He's kind. Keep him" at the barbecue read as forgetfulness. Verdict: drop.

items.title: 6.14 "The recruiter's email" in v6 The vet
items.html: PLACEHOLDER, yours. Fix when drafting, as the addendum says. James's minute of connecting papers after Noor says "Kalder" needs a new first link in place of the recruiter. The seat contract "through Kalder's consultancy" in The money is that link, and it is already in v8.2. Verdict: keep, changed.
